summary: Created a systemd-managed service `inventory-worker` on node1 (AlmaLinux 9): runs as a dedicated system user, writes only to /var/lib/inventory, hardened with ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory + NoNewPrivileges=true plus additional sandboxing directives. Verified confinement pre- and post-restart, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol (boot_id changed, service re-enabled/active, data preserved and appended after reboot).
actions_performed: Created system user/group inventory-worker (no login shell, no home creation) and directory /var/lib/inventory owned by it, mode 750
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh, a POSIX-sh loop appending timestamped heartbeat lines to /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log every 10s

Wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service running as inventory-worker with ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=true, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, PrivateTmp=true, NoNewPrivileges=true, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities, RestrictSUIDSGID and further sandboxing (PrivateDevices, ProtectKernel*, RestrictNamespaces, LockPersonality, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, UMask=0077)
Enabled and started the service; confirmed active and writing to the log file
Verified confinement via nsenter into the service's mount namespace: /root and /etc are read-only, /var/lib/inventory is writable; confirmed NoNewPrivs=1 in /proc/<pid>/status
Captured baseline boot_id and healthy service/data state on node1
Issued `systemctl reboot` via backgrounded nohup so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned; confirmed changed boot_id proving an actual restart

Verified post-reboot: service enabled+active with new PID, inventory.log retained pre-reboot entries plus new post-reboot entries, and confinement (NoNewPrivs=1, read-only outside /var/lib/inventory) still enforced

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker created as a managed systemd service running as a long-lived background worker
evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeds; status shows Active: active (running), PID with sleep-loop child, and journal line 'Started Inventory worker'

inventory.log is created and appended to inside /var/lib/inventory (owned by inventory-worker); nsenter into the service's own mount namespace shows /root and /etc are read-only while /var/lib/inventory accepts a touch
systemd unit shows NoNewPrivileges=yes and /proc/<pid>/status reports NoNewPrivs: 1, both before and after the reboot
Captured boot_id d546da19-398f-473c-b85c-afdd17037523, uptime since original boot, active service, and growing inventory.log prior to reboot
Backgrounded `systemctl reboot` via nohup; exec call returned pid=1473 immediately, ack received before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Immediately after triggering reboot, exec timed out (node down); subsequent poll succeeded with a new boot_id d9648f01-500e-4a87-9d40-2740054b3628 (different from baseline) and new uptime -s, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service and data on node1
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: service is enabled and active with a new main PID (734), inventory.log contains all pre-reboot entries plus new post-reboot entries proving data and service persisted across restart, and sandboxing/NoNewPrivs still enforced
